definitions.explanation: Sweet foods or snacks; includes candy, cookies, cakes, etc.

examples.japanese: お{菓子|かし}を⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧。
お{菓子|かし}が⟦{好|す}き→好き：02355_suki⟧です。
⟦お{土産|みやげ}→お土産：01353_omiyage⟧にお{菓子|かし}をもらった。
examples.english: I received sweets as a souvenir.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧たちにお{菓子|かし}を⟦あげた→あげる：00546_ageru⟧。
この⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧のお{菓子|かし}はとても⟦{人気|にんき}→人気：01488_ninki⟧がある。
examples.english: The sweets at this shop are very popular.

notes:
お{菓子|かし} is a general term for sweets, snacks, and confections.

TYPES:
- ⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧: traditional Japanese sweets
- ⟦{洋菓子|ようがし}→洋菓子：04998_yougashi⟧: Western-style sweets
- {駄菓子|だがし}: cheap candy (nostalgic treats)
- {生菓子|なまがし}: fresh confections

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- お{菓子|かし}を⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧: to make sweets
- お{菓子|かし}{屋|や}: confectionery shop
- ⟦{手作|てづく}り→手作り：08300_tezukuri⟧のお{菓子|かし}: homemade sweets
- お{菓子|かし}{作|づく}り: making sweets

USAGE:
The お prefix (honorific) is commonly used but can be dropped: {菓子|かし}. In compounds, お is usually omitted: ⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧, {菓子|かし}{折|おり} (box of sweets).
